summary.short: Kentucky statute, added as new sections of KRS Chapter 367, giving Kentucky consumers data rights and imposing controller and processor duties on businesses meeting volume thresholds, enforced by the Attorney General. Effective January 1, 2026; impact-assessment duties apply to processing created on or after June 1, 2026.
summary.long: House Bill 15 (2024) adds Sections 1 to 10 to KRS Chapter 367 as the Kentucky Consumer Data Protection Act. Sections 1 to 10 apply to persons that conduct business in the Commonwealth or target products or services to its residents and that control or process personal data of at least 100,000 consumers in a calendar year, or 25,000 consumers while deriving over 50% of gross revenue from selling personal data. Government bodies, financial institutions under Gramm-Leach-Bliley, HIPAA covered entities and business associates, nonprofits, higher education institutions, certain utilities, and listed categories of data are exempt. Consumers may request access, correction, deletion, portability, and opt-out of targeted advertising, data sales, and profiling in furtherance of decisions with legal or similarly significant effects; controllers must respond within 45 days, extendable once by 45 days. Controllers must limit collection, maintain security, avoid unlawful discrimination, obtain consent for sensitive data, publish privacy notices, disclose sales and targeted advertising, and offer request mechanisms. Processors must follow contract terms on confidentiality, deletion, information and assessments. Controllers must conduct and document data protection impact assessments for targeted advertising, data sales, certain profiling, sensitive data and heightened-risk processing, which the Attorney General may request. The Attorney General has exclusive enforcement authority, must give 30 days' written notice with a cure opportunity, may seek damages up to $7,500 per continued violation, and no private right of action is created. Civil penalties go to a consumer privacy fund administered by the Attorney General. The Act takes effect January 1, 2026.

relations.note: Each of Sections 1 to 10 is created as a new section of KRS Chapter 367; the Act adds provisions rather than rewriting existing sections.
